prompt: A real astronaut photograph of Earth taken from the International Space Station in low orbit, about 400 km up, with a rectilinear lens. The curved limb of the Earth runs across the top third of the frame: a thin glowing blue atmosphere line with black space above it. Below, the planet is almost entirely covered by thick bright white cloud: large fields of cumulus and a solid continuous cloud deck with soft shading and texture fill the centre and most of the frame. Only a little warm desert and deep blue ocean show through a few small gaps near the lower corners, far from the centre. Natural daylight, natural colour, no text, no spacecraft parts. The result is a real, unretouched camera photograph: natural rock, soil, sand and plants with fine weathered detail and irregular natural edges, real sunlight and soft atmospheric haze on distant landforms, like a professional landscape photo.
